summary:
Sort, then move two pointers inward: when the pair sum is below the target, only a bigger left value can get
closer, and when it's above, only a smaller right value can. Track the best sum (closer, or equally close and
smaller). O(n log n).

question.md:
Return the sum of two different elements that is closest to `target`; on a tie, the smaller sum.

- **Values up to ±10⁹ and target up to ±2 × 10⁹**: distances need 64-bit arithmetic.
- **Up to 10⁵ elements.**

think.md:
`[8, -4, 15, 3, -9, 6]`, target 5. The closest sums are [4, 6, 2]…, so the answer is **4**.

After sorting, look at the smallest and largest values. If their sum is below the target, the smallest value
paired with anything else would be even smaller, so it has no better pairing left: move past it. Symmetrically
for a sum above the target. Every pair that could be the closest is still visited.

approaches.title: Every pair

idea.md: Check every pair, keeping the best by (distance, sum).

build: Compare (|s − target|, s) with the best.

notes.java: A huge sentinel, far from any target.

lines.text: Closer wins; on equal distance, the smaller sum. 64-bit so `s − target` can't overflow.
A sum of two values within ±10⁹ fits in an `int`, so the answer can be returned as one.

walk.title: Try every pair, keeping the sum closest to the target (smaller sum on a tie).

limits.md: 5 × 10⁹ pairs for 10⁵ values. After sorting, two pointers visit only O(n) candidate pairs, and the skipped ones are provably no closer.

approaches.title: Sort and squeeze

idea.md: Sort. `i = 0`, `j = n − 1`. Compute `s`, update the best; if `s < target` move `i` right, if `s > target` move `j` left, if equal return `s`.

build: Two pointers; update best by (distance, sum).

lines.text: Pointers at both ends; no best yet.
The current pair's sum, in 64 bits.
Keep it if closer, or equally close and smaller.
Below the target, `a[i]` has no closer partner left (all are ≤ `a[j]`): drop it. Above, drop `a[j]`. Exact hits can't be beaten.

complexity.md: **Time O(n log n)** for the sort; the squeeze is O(n). **Space O(n)** for the copy.

steps.text: -9 + 8 = -1 (distance 6). Below the target: move i right.
-4 + 8 = 4 (distance 1). Below the target: move i right.

walk.title: Sort, then squeeze from both ends: below the target, raise the sum; above it, lower it.

takeaways.md:
- **Closest pair sum = sort + squeeze**; the moving rule is the same as for an exact target.
- Track ties explicitly (here: smaller sum wins).
- Compute differences in 64 bits when values and targets are near the 32-bit limit.
